gui.reason: Surfaces on the Gameplay page of the PS2 Madden 09 Studio as four spin controls -- formations, sets, plays per book, plays per set -- each floored at the cap this executable already enforces and ceilinged at 65534, the largest a 16-bit sltiu immediate can carry. A cap left at its floor writes no word. Beside the controls the page repeats the lane's own sentence about what the patch does not do: these are the editor's checks only, the shipped tables are packed exactly full, and nothing has been booted. The other six catalogue rows are subject areas with no located site: their controls are drawn read-only rather than offering a switch that could only refuse, and translation refuses each by name.

input_constraints: Five 32-bit words at fixed EE addresses, and only each sltiu instruction's 16-bit immediate changes; the opcode and both register fields are carried through from the word the executable already holds.

Every original word is read from the user's own boot ELF three times over -- when the catalogue is built, again when the plan is made, and a third time by the independent verifier -- and any mismatch refuses before anything is written.

A cap below the one this executable already enforces is refused, because books the disc ships already hold more rows than the editor's cap and shrinking the check would strand them; a cap above 65534 is refused because its immediate would not fit.

Delivery is a pnach beside the image by default; the on-disc route writes the same words into SLUS_217.70 on a NEW image through the shared fixed-allocation ISO9660 writer, which is safe only because a word replacement never changes the executable's length.
The six other catalogue rows carry no address, offset or code byte at all: no site has been located for any of them and translation refuses each by name.

Retail-free apart from the translation table itself -- five addresses and five words, which are the deliverable exactly as they would be in a hand-written pnach. Everything else is read from the user's own image at run time.
portme: Raising the editor caps is the first of two layers. The second -- the database library's own per-table capacity -- is not shipped: table_set_capacity at 0x0082A6A0 is a subroutine, not an immediate, five of its six callers hand it the capacity they just read out of the table object, and the header loader fills that from each table's on-disc max_records. Adding it needs new code at a hook site the owner's research records as located but not pinned, and new code cannot be verified without a boot.
Promoting this row to runtime-proved needs the patch witnessed in an emulator: open the create-a-playbook editor on a shipped 20-set book and try to add a 21st set. Nothing here has been booted.
Locate a site for one of the six proposed patches and fill in a single TRANSLATIONS entry with its test; nothing else in the lane changes, which is what the synthetic-ELF proof exists to guarantee.

public_distribution.rule: Ship the lane, the shared PS2 boot-ELF and ISO9660 readers and writer it uses, their self-tests and the synthetic sources CI proves them on, plus user-authored cap recipes and the emitted pnach text. The user's ISO, the executable inside it and any patched image stay with the user.

runtime.scope: Offline only: words proven, nothing seen. The five original words were read out of both the retail (PCSX2 CRC 38014255) and the Deluxe (084562FF) executables and decoded independently; the two editions hold the same word at all five addresses, and the nine words in which those two executables differ are all elsewhere. The emitted pnach and the on-disc image were both verified by re-reading the user's own ELF, and the disc route additionally proves that every byte of the new image outside the five declared four-byte ranges is identical to the source. No emulator was run and no frame was rendered. The runtime witness this row is waiting for is the create-a-playbook editor accepting a 21st set on a shipped 20-set book -- which is expected to fail until the library-capacity layer exists, and that expectation is itself untested.

gui.reason: Surfaces on the Text & Team Identity page of the PS2 Madden 09 Studio as an editor, one target per NFL team -- 32 on the retail image. Each offers the four names the record carries, the two colours as colour pickers, and the city id; the four fields whose meaning is only a hypothesis are read and deliberately not drawn. Budgets are on screen (a name's is its field's bytes less the terminator: 16, 17, 6 and 16 characters), refusals are inline, a dry run resolves every edit before any image exists, the build writes a NEW image, and the lane's independent verifier gives the verdict. Bytes proven; nothing has been seen in-game -- no rebuilt Madden 09 disc has been booted in an emulator, so no claim is made about what the game draws on a team-select screen.

input_constraints: One target is a team, not a record: a rename is written into every copy of the TEAM row the disc's own databases agree on -- the DB_TEAMS.DAT member and the row of the bare STRMDATA.DB whose TGID matches -- in one recipe, so the two cannot be left disagreeing. STRMDATA.DB's rows are not in TGID order, so the second copy is resolved by reading the field and never by arithmetic.

A copy that does not already agree is left alone and the receipt says which field made it differ; a guess dressed as consistency is not written. On the retail disc all 32 teams' two copies agree, so 64 rows are written for 32 edited teams.

TEMPLATE.DAT member 1 carries a third copy of all 32 teams, byte-identical, and is NOT written: TEMPLATE.DAT is named in the FE.QKL preload cache, which carries a copy of at least some of what it names. The list is read off the user's own image rather than a table written down here, and DB_TEAMS.DAT and STRMDATA.DB are named in neither cache.

Eleven fields, named: TDNA (17 bytes), TLNA (18), TSNA (7) and TMNC (17) as latin-1 text NUL-padded to the field, one byte short of the width so the terminator survives; TBCR/TBCG/TBCB and TB2R/TB2G/TB2B as two colours of three one-byte channels, with a colour word's alpha dropped and said to be dropped; CYID as an 8-bit index. TCDO, TCRP, TGPT and TCTX were read and are not offered -- the owner's research records them as a hypothesis, and a hypothesis does not belong in an editor.

Fixed allocation, twice over: a TDB field owns a fixed run of bits in a fixed-stride record, so a record edit cannot change a length, and the ISO writer replaces a file only inside the extent it already owns. All four CRC-32/MPEG-2 checksum sites are recomputed on every write and re-derived from the destination's own bytes by the verifier, which imports none of the writer and fails on a byte changed outside the declared ranges, on a record changed behind the receipt's back, on a stale checksum, and on a name that does not pad out its own field.
portme: Real-disc trial: DB_TEAMS.DAT member 0's team -- its abbreviation and its primary colour -- wrote both copies (the member's TEAM record 0 and STRMDATA.DB's TEAM record 106, matched by TGID and not by position), declared 7,746,536 bytes in four ranges, and the verifier passed with 8 values read back, 2 databases re-parsed, 470 checksum slots correct and 1,649,593,368 unchanged bytes compared across 197 entries of two 1,657,339,904-byte images.
A runtime witness would be a PCSX2 boot of a rebuilt image showing the renamed abbreviation on the Team Select screen and the recoloured helmet and jersey in its preview.

Not offered yet: the team's stadium and city NAME, which live in STAD and CITY tables in TEMPLATE.DAT only -- a preload-cached container -- so a full relocation spans two files and two schemas this row does not attempt; the 202 historical squads and the free-agent pool in DB_TEAMS.DAT members 32..234; and the team names spelled as prose in the story banks, which the Menus & UI page's text lane edits string by string.

runtime.scope: Offline only: bytes proven, pixels not; nothing has been on a screen. The real-disc trial changed one team's abbreviation and primary colour and wrote both of the disc's agreeing copies -- DB_TEAMS.DAT member 0's TEAM record 0 and STRMDATA.DB's TEAM record 106 -- declaring 7,746,536 bytes in four ranges (each file's whole extent and its directory record's 8-byte length field). The independent verifier passed: every edited value read back from the destination, all 470 checksum slots of the two edited databases correct, every byte of each database that differed inside a declared field span or a checksum slot, every written name padded out to its own field, and ps2_iso9660_verify comparing 197 entries and 1,649,593,368 unchanged bytes of the two 1,657,339,904-byte images. Two adversarial flips on that same destination were both refused: one byte outside every declared range, and one inside a declared ISO range. No PCSX2 run. A runtime witness would be a boot showing the renamed abbreviation on Team Select and the recoloured jersey preview.

gui.reason: Surfaces on the Menus & UI page of the PS2 Madden 09 Studio as an editor. Each target is one string slot inside a bank, addressed by its byte offset; the budget on screen is that slot's own allocation, a shorter replacement is padded with the format's terminator, and a longer one is refused with the length it has to fit. A dry run resolves every edit before any image exists, the build writes a NEW image, and the lane's independent verifier gives the verdict. Bytes proven; nothing has been seen in-game -- no rebuilt Madden 09 disc has been booted in an emulator, so no claim is made about how the game draws the replacement.

input_constraints: Fixed allocation: a replacement is written inside the slot's own bytes and padded to them with NULs, so the member, its container and the image all keep their exact length. A longer replacement is refused with the length it must fit.

Six containers are editable -- OSDKSTRN.DAT and the five story banks. GAMEDATA.DAT, LOADDATA.DAT and STADATA.DAT are named in the FE.QKL and GAME.QKL preload caches, which carry a copy of at least some of what they name, so editing one copy and not the other is refused; the list is read off the user's own image rather than a table written down here.

The catalogue document is still counts, lengths and digests and carries no string, which a test asserts by searching the serialised document for the fixture's own strings; the strings reach a screen only through the targets built from the user's image and through an explicit preview.
Strings are encoded latin-1, never utf-8: EA stores 8-bit characters. A replacement carrying a NUL is refused -- that byte is what ends a string here.

The source is opened read-only and never written; the destination must not already exist and may not be the source. An edit made against a string that has since changed is refused on its digest rather than written over. The verifier imports none of the writer and fails on any byte changed outside the edited slots.
portme: Real-disc trial: one 50,519-byte slot of OSDKSTRN.DAT member 0 replaced, declaring 741,088 bytes in two ranges; the verifier passed with 1,656,598,816 unchanged bytes compared across 197 entries, and failed when one byte outside every declared range was flipped.
A runtime witness would be a PCSX2 boot of a rebuilt image showing the replaced string drawn, and showing that a menu which lays out from a measured width does not re-flow when a string shortens.

On this disc a bank is usually one string with no NUL in it, so its slot is the whole member: replacing it replaces the whole bank. A finer unit -- the pipe-delimited KEY=value pairs OSDKSTRN.DAT carries, say -- would need that inner grammar decoded, which has not been done.
Group the story generator's banks by their role so a user can find the one they mean without opening each in turn.

gui.reason: Surfaced on the Uniforms & Equipment page of the PS2 Madden 09 Studio beside the export row: pick a texture, give back a PNG of exactly its size, and Build writes a NEW disc image. The page repeats the row's own sentence -- no rebuilt Madden 09 container has ever been booted -- so the user is told what the offline proof does and does not cover before they build anything.

input_constraints: Read-only source: the ISO is opened for reading and never modified. The destination is a NEW image that must not exist, and naming the source as the destination is refused.

A PNG must be exactly the texture's own size, 8-bit, non-interlaced, RGB or RGBA. A whole-number multiple can be exported and looked at but not written back, and the refusal names the size that was wanted.

A texture rides its own CLUT: the PNG is indexed against the palette the member already carries, so a colour that palette does not hold cannot be introduced. The receipt says how many pixels landed exactly and the worst channel any pixel moved by.

An unchanged pixel keeps the index byte the file used. 420 of the disc's 1,780 MMAP members carry a CLUT with a duplicate colour, so indexing from pixels alone has more than one right answer; keeping the original index is what makes a rewrite touch only what the artist touched.

Fixed allocation by default: the rebuilt container goes back inside the extent it already owns whenever it fits, and the image keeps its length. Only when it does not fit is the ISO writer's opt-in growth used, and the receipt then names the appended sectors.

The independent verifier imports nothing that wrote the image: tools/ps2_iso9660_verify.py re-derives every declared byte with its own ISO9660 decoder, every untouched member of the container is compared byte for byte, and each rewritten texture is decoded out of the NEW image and measured against the PNG the user handed in.
Retail-free: no decoded pixel, member byte or palette entry from any game is in this repository. CI proves the whole path on a synthetic disc.
portme: Boot a rebuilt container in PCSX2 and see the game load it. That is the only thing between this row and runtime-proved, and it needs the rig.
Capture a GS dump of Madden 09 so replacement_identity can name a PCSX2 file; the pack route stays refused until then, and it is a different row.
IPU1: the 1,188 version-1 members of UIS_MCFL.DAT are refused by name at both ends, read and write.
Mip levels below the largest keep the art they had. A caller that wants them rebuilt passes them itself through mmap_art.encode; no filter is chosen here.

public_distribution.rule: Ship the lane, the shared EA TERF reader and writer, the ISO9660 writer and its independent verifier, their self-tests and the synthetic sources CI proves them on; the user's ISO and every byte read out of it stay with the user.

runtime.scope: Offline only. Every step is proved against the user's own bytes -- the member decodes back to the pixels that were given, the container keeps the layout rules the retail discs follow, every untouched member is byte-identical, and the image-level verifier re-derives every declared byte from the two files -- and NO rebuilt Madden 09 container has ever been booted in an emulator or on hardware. That the game loads the result is not claimed anywhere.

capabilities.summary: Write an edited PNG back into a Madden 09 disc's MMAP textures, producing a NEW image. Three encoders had to exist first and all three are proved offline: an LZH1 encoder (codec 5, no public encoder existed) whose output every LZH1 member of the disc's art containers decodes back from byte for byte under two independent decoders, and which comes out at about EA's own size; an MMAP member writer that lays out a member's tables and offsets afresh and reproduces all 1,780 members of the four art containers byte for byte from their own decoded pixels; and an opt-in relocation mode in the ISO9660 writer for the case where a rebuilt container will not fit the extent it owns. Fixed allocation is still the default and the ordinary outcome. The receipt names the codec chosen per member, the pixels that landed exactly, and whether the image grew. NOT booted: no rebuilt Madden 09 container has been loaded by the game, and nothing here claims otherwise.

gui.reason: Surfaced on the Uniforms & Equipment page of the PS2 Madden 09 Studio with preview, Export PNG and a checked Import PNG, and with Write PCSX2 pack still not offered: the replacement filenames are known for 3,024 textures now, but no pack built from them has been loaded. Export is the value today. The independent verifier re-decodes every exported texture from the user's own disc by key -- not through the catalogue that produced the receipt -- and fails on a tampered file or an undeclared one.

input_constraints: Read-only source: the ISO is opened for reading and never modified; the export is a NEW folder that must not already exist, and the source may not be named as the destination.
The catalogue carries dimensions, formats, counts and file names -- never a pixel. Pixels are decoded when a texture is previewed or exported, straight from the user's own image.

An import is checked, never silently resized: a PNG must be exactly the texture's size or an exact whole-number multiple of it, 8-bit, non-interlaced, RGB or RGBA. Anything else is refused naming the size that was wanted.

A same-size PNG is indexed against the texture's OWN palette and the result reported: a Madden 09 texture rides its own CLUT, so a colour that palette does not carry cannot be introduced, and the user is told how many pixels landed exactly.

replacement_identity answers for a texture a PCSX2 dump has been seen drawing and None for one it has not. The name is built from hashes the emulator computes at draw time, so tools/madden09_ps2_texture_identities.py learns it by pairing a dump with this disc on exact pixels; 3,024 textures have one today. The Write PCSX2 pack step is still not offered: what is proved is the pairing, not that the emulator loads a pack.
Version-1 MMAP members store their pixels under EA codec 4 (IPU1), which nothing here decodes; all 1,188 of them are refused by name rather than exported wrong.
portme: Load a pack built from these names in PCSX2 and see the replacement drawn; that is the only thing between the identity table and a pack writer, and it needs the rig.
Join the uniform members to teams. UNIFORMS.DAT names none of its 455 members or their images, so which team a member belongs to is not established; the executable's own tables are the place to look.
Decode IPU1 so the 1,188 memory-card front-end textures can be exported too.
Writing a texture back into the container needs an LZH1 encoder and one rebuilt disc booted; neither exists, and until they do this stays extract-only.

public_distribution.rule: Ship the lane, the shared EA TERF and EA TDB readers it imports, their self-tests and the synthetic sources CI proves them on; the user's ISO and every byte read out of it stay with the user.

runtime.scope: Extract-only: the exporter creates local PNGs and no path writes anything into the game or the emulator, so there is no runtime behaviour to witness. That PCSX2 would render these textures identically is NOT claimed. A texture dump of the game running now exists and the exported pixels pair with it exactly, which is evidence about the decode; no pack has been loaded, which is the gap that stops the pack writer. The evidence for the decode is that the exported PNGs are recognisable art when looked at, not that the game draws them.

capabilities.summary: Decode the MMAP textures on a user's SLUS-21770 disc and export them as PNGs. An MMAP member is a table-of-tables -- an image table, a surface table of mip levels, a palette table and a name table -- whose pixels are 4- or 8-bit indexed, sometimes packed again under EA codec LZM1 inside a member the container already unpacked, with 256-entry CLUTs in the PS2 GS's CSM1 interleave. Measured on the retail disc's four art containers: 1,780 texture members, 7,616 images, 7,082 decodable; across ten containers 11,039 of 12,779 images decode and every refusal falls in three named groups. The decode is proved by looking at the result -- recognisable jersey sheets, legible number fonts and human faces, not plausible noise. Nothing is written to the disc.
